Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=0]$ given that $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|0}=1.$

current_example.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\dfrac{3}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ |

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=1\big]$ given that $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is $\mu_{Y|1} = \dfrac{9}{4}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find $f_{Y | X}(y \,|\, x),$ let's first find the marginal distribution for $X,$ corresponding to the row totals: 

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | $f_X(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ | $\dfrac{2}{5}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\dfrac{3}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{3}{5}$ |

The conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x$ is

$$
f_{Y | X}(y \,|\, x)  = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)}.
$$

Therefore, dividing each joint probability by the corresponding row total, we obtain the conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x{:}$

| $f_{Y | X}(y \,|\, x)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ | $\dfrac{1}{2}$ | $1$ |
| $X=2$ | $\dfrac{1}{2}$ | $\dfrac{1}{3}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $1$ |

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=1] & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)]-{\mu }_{Y|1}^{2} \\  & =[{1}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}+{2}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}+{3}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}]-{(\frac{9}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+1+\frac{9}{2}-\frac{81}{16} \\  & =\frac{11}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
